claim: Axon projection is a spatial- and temporal-specific process in which the growth cone receives environmental signals guiding axons to their final destination.
source: Axon projection is a spatial- and temporal-specific process in which the growth cone receives environmental signals guiding axons to their final destination.
evidence: This is a general statement about axon projection that draws from established scientific understanding of the process.

claim: s-LNv axons undergo an initial vertical projection in the early larval stage.
source: Our findings reveal that these axons undergo an initial vertical projection in the early larval stage, followed by a subsequent transition to a horizontal projection in the early-to-mid third instar larvae.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations and data presented in the manuscript showing the developmental trajectory of s-LNv axons.

claim: s-LNv axons transition to a horizontal projection in the early-to-mid third instar larvae.
source: Our findings reveal that these axons undergo an initial vertical projection in the early larval stage, followed by a subsequent transition to a horizontal projection in the early-to-mid third instar larvae.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations and quantitative data showing the timing of the directional transition.

claim: The vertical projection of s-LNv axons correlates with mushroom body calyx expansion.
source: The vertical projection of s-LNv axons correlates with mushroom body calyx expansion, while the s-LNv-expressed Down syndrome cell adhesion molecule (Dscam1) interacts with Netrins to regulate the horizontal projection.
evidence: This claim is supported by correlation analysis and experimental data showing the relationship between MB calyx growth and s-LNv vertical projection.

claim: s-LNv-expressed Dscam1 interacts with Netrins to regulate the horizontal projection.
source: The vertical projection of s-LNv axons correlates with mushroom body calyx expansion, while the s-LNv-expressed Down syndrome cell adhesion molecule (Dscam1) interacts with Netrins to regulate the horizontal projection.
evidence: This claim is supported by genetic manipulation experiments showing the role of Dscam1 and Netrins in horizontal projection.

claim: Locally newborn dorsal clock neurons secrete Netrins during a specific temporal window.
source: During a specific temporal window, locally newborn dorsal clock neurons secrete Netrins, facilitating the transition of axonal projection direction in s-LNvs.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data showing NetB expression in newborn DNs at specific developmental timepoints.

claim: DN-secreted Netrins facilitate the transition of axonal projection direction in s-LNvs.
source: During a specific temporal window, locally newborn dorsal clock neurons secrete Netrins, facilitating the transition of axonal projection direction in s-LNvs.
evidence: This claim is supported by genetic experiments including DN ablation and Netrin rescue experiments.

claim: The growth cone is specialized at the tip of the extending axon and is critical for receiving multiple guidance signals from the external environment to guide axon projection.
source: The growth cone, which is specialized at the tip of the extending axon, is critical for receiving multiple guidance signals from the external environment to guide axon projection (Agi et al., 2024; Lowery and Van Vactor, 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature on growth cone function.

claim: Guidance cues regulate cytoskeletal dynamics through growth cone-specific receptors, steering axons via attractive or repulsive signals.
source: Guidance cues regulate cytoskeletal dynamics through growth cone-specific receptors, steering axons via attractive or repulsive signals (Tessier-Lavigne and Goodman, 1996; Araújo and Tear, 2003; Koch et al., 2012; Kolodkin and Tessier-Lavigne, 2011; Stoeckli, 2018; Zang et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to established literature on axon guidance mechanisms.

claim: Several guidance cues have been identified and divided into four classical families: Semaphorins, Ephrins, Netrins, and Slits.
source: Over the last 30 years, several guidance cues have been identified and divided into four classical families: Semaphorins (Kolodkin et al., 1992; Luo et al., 1993; Pasterkamp, 2012; Raper, 2000; Winberg et al., 1998), Ephrins (Cheng et al., 1995; Kania and Klein, 2016; Sperry, 1963; Wilkinson, 2001), Netrins (Colamarino and Tessier-Lavigne, 1995; Hong et al., 1999; Kennedy et al., 1994; Meijers et al., 2020; Pan et al., 2023; Serafini et al., 1994), and Slits (Agi et al., 2024; Battye et al., 1999; Kidd et al., 1999; Seeger et al., 1993; Tessier-Lavigne and Goodman, 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by extensive citations to the literature establishing these guidance cue families.

claim: Immunoreactivity for pigment-dispersing factor (PDF) is initially detected in the brains of first-instar larvae 4–5 hr after larval hatching.
source: Immunoreactivity for pigment-dispersing factor (PDF) (Cyran et al., 2005), representing the pattern of LNv neurons, is initially detected in the brains of first-instar larvae 4–5 hr after larval hatching (ALH) (Helfrich-Förster, 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work by Helfrich-Förster, 1997.

claim: At 8 hr ALH, the GFP signal strongly co-localized with the PDF signal within the axons.
source: At 8 hr ALH, the green fluorescent protein (GFP) signal strongly co-localized with the PDF signal within the axons (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The vertical projection distance of the s-LNvs axon increases linearly as larval development progresses.
source: Statistical analyses revealed a steadfast linear increase in the vertical projection distance of the s-LNvs axon as larval development progressed (Figure 1A, B).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements and statistical analysis shown in Figure 1B.

claim: At 8, 24, 48, and 72 hr ALH, the A.U. value for s-LNvs axon projection in the horizontal direction remained relatively stable at approximately 0.13.
source: Remarkably, at the time points of 8, 24, 48, and 72 hr ALH, the A.U. value for s-LNvs axon projection in the horizontal direction remained relatively stable at approximately 0.13.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements shown in Figure 1C.

claim: At 96 and 120 hr ALH, the A.U. value for s-LNvs axon horizontal projection increased to approximately 0.25.
source: However, at 96 and 120 hr ALH, a significant and striking increase in the A.U. value ensued, eventually reaching approximately 0.25 (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The transition of s-LNv axon projection from vertical toward the horizontal direction occurs in the early-to-mid third instar larvae, specifically during 72–96 hr ALH.
source: These findings suggest that the precise transition of s-LNv axon projection from vertical toward the horizontal direction occurs in the early-to-mid third instar larvae, specifically during 72–96 hr ALH (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by the temporal analysis of axon projection shown in Figure 1.

claim: The axons of s-LNv project dorsally, coming in close proximity to the dendritic tree of the mushroom body, specifically the calyx.
source: The axons of s-LNv project dorsally, coming in close proximity to the dendritic tree of the mushroom body (MB), specifically the calyx (Figure 2A, C).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data showing the spatial relationship between s-LNv axons and MB calyx.

claim: MB predominantly comprises 2500 intrinsic neurons, known as Kenyon Cells (KCs).
source: MB predominantly comprises 2500 intrinsic neurons, known as Kenyon Cells (KCs) (Puñal et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Puñal et al., 2021.

claim: The γ cells emerge from the embryonic stage until early third-instar larval phase.
source: The γ cells emerge from the embryonic stage until early third-instar larval phase, while the α′/β′ cells are born during the latter half of larval life, and the α/β cells appear in the post-larval stage (Lee et al., 1999; Puñal et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Lee et al., 1999 and Puñal et al., 2021.

claim: The α′/β′ cells are born during the latter half of larval life.
source: The γ cells emerge from the embryonic stage until early third-instar larval phase, while the α′/β′ cells are born during the latter half of larval life, and the α/β cells appear in the post-larval stage (Lee et al., 1999; Puñal et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Lee et al., 1999 and Puñal et al., 2021.

claim: The α/β cells appear in the post-larval stage.
source: The γ cells emerge from the embryonic stage until early third-instar larval phase, while the α′/β′ cells are born during the latter half of larval life, and the α/β cells appear in the post-larval stage (Lee et al., 1999; Puñal et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Lee et al., 1999 and Puñal et al., 2021.

claim: The calyx area increases proportionally with the advancement of developmental time, demonstrating a linear relationship.
source: Statistical analyses further confirmed that the calyx area increased proportionally with the advancement of developmental time, demonstrating a linear relationship (Figure 2B, C).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Pearson correlation analysis revealed a robust positive correlation between the calyx area and the vertical projection distance of s-LNvs axon (r = 0.9987, p < 0.0001 for OK107-GAL4; r = 0.9963, p = 0.0003 for Tab2-201Y-GAL4).
source: Additionally, Pearson correlation analysis unveiled a robust positive correlation between the calyx area and the vertical projection distance of s-LNvs axon (r = 0.9987, p < 0.0001 for OK107-GAL4; r = 0.9963, p = 0.0003 for Tab2-201Y-GAL4) (Figure 2B, C).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical correlation analysis presented in Figure 2B.

claim: In the ablation group, there was a noticeable decrease in vertical projection distance at 48 hr ALH.
source: However, in the ablation group, although the initial vertical projection of s-LNvs appeared normal, there was a noticeable decrease in vertical projection distance at 48 hr ALH.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from MB ablation experiments shown in Figure 2D, E.

claim: The vertical projection distance in the ablation group measured only 20–30 µm at 72 hr ALH.
source: This vertical development trend ceased thereafter, with the vertical projection distance measuring only 20–30 µm at 72 hr ALH (Figure 2D, E).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements from ablation experiments shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Knockdown of Dscam1 resulted in a notable decrease in the horizontal projection distance of s-LNv axons in late third instar larvae and adults.
source: Significantly, the knockdown of Down syndrome cell adhesion molecule (Dscam1) resulted in a notable decrease in the horizontal projection distance of s-LNv axons in late third instar larvae and adults (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNAi knockdown experiments shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: At 96 hr ALH, vertical projection showed no significant changes in Pdf-GAL4;UAS-Dscam1-RNAi flies.
source: At 96 hr ALH, vertical projection showed no significant changes in Pdf-GAL4;UAS-Dscam1-RNAi flies, but a noticeable deficit was observed in the horizontal projection of the s-LNvs axon (Figure 3A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements shown in Figure 3B.

claim: A noticeable deficit was observed in the horizontal projection of the s-LNvs axon in Pdf-GAL4;UAS-Dscam1-RNAi flies at 96 hr ALH.
source: At 96 hr ALH, vertical projection showed no significant changes in Pdf-GAL4;UAS-Dscam1-RNAi flies, but a noticeable deficit was observed in the horizontal projection of the s-LNvs axon (Figure 3A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Dscam1 specifically regulates the horizontal projection of s-LNvs axon.
source: These observations strongly indicate that Dscam1 specifically regulates the horizontal projection of s-LNvs axon.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental results showing selective effects on horizontal but not vertical projection.

claim: Trans-heterozygous Dscam1 mutants and homozygotes exhibited shortened horizontal axon projection.
source: While all heterozygous mutants displayed normal horizontal axon projection in s-LNvs, trans-heterozygous mutants and homozygotes exhibited shortened horizontal axon projection (Figure 3D, E).
evidence: This claim is supported by genetic analysis of Dscam1 mutants shown in Figure 3D, E.

claim: Immunostaining results indicated concentrated Dscam1 expression at the growth cone of s-LNv axons in third-instar larvae.
source: Additionally, our immunostaining results indicated concentrated Dscam1 expression at the growth cone of s-LNv axons in third-instar larvae (Figure 3F).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Dscam1 controls the horizontal axon projection of s-LNvs in a cell-autonomous manner.
source: Taken together, these data demonstrate that Dscam1 controls the horizontal axon projection of s-LNvs in a cell-autonomous manner.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combination of cell-specific knockdown and mutant analysis experiments.

claim: Dscam1 is a well-recognized cell adhesion molecule that plays a crucial role in axon guidance.
source: Dscam1 is a well-recognized cell adhesion molecule that plays a crucial role in axon guidance (Chen et al., 2006; Hummel et al., 2003; Zhan et al., 2004; Zhang et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature on Dscam1 function.

claim: Knockdown of tsr and chic in s-LNvs recaptured the horizontal axon projection deficits in Dscam1 knockdown flies or Dscam1 mutants.
source: Convincingly, knockdown of the cytoskeletal molecules tsr (the Drosophila homolog of cofilin) (Sudarsanam et al., 2020) and chic (the Drosophila homolog of profilin) (Shields et al., 2014) in s-LNvs recaptured the horizontal axon projection deficits in Dscam1 knockdown flies or Dscam1 mutants (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, D).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNAi knockdown experiments shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Knockdown of Dock and Pak phenocopied Dscam1 knockdown flies or Dscam1 mutants.
source: Consistently, knockdown of Dock and Pak, the guidance receptor partners of Dscam1 (Schmucker et al., 2000), or SH3PX1, the critical linker between Dscam1 and the cytoskeleton (Worby et al., 2001), phenocopied Dscam1 knockdown flies or Dscam1 mutants (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A, B).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNAi knockdown experiments shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A, B.

claim: Knockdown of SH3PX1 phenocopied Dscam1 knockdown flies or Dscam1 mutants.
source: Consistently, knockdown of Dock and Pak, the guidance receptor partners of Dscam1 (Schmucker et al., 2000), or SH3PX1, the critical linker between Dscam1 and the cytoskeleton (Worby et al., 2001), phenocopied Dscam1 knockdown flies or Dscam1 mutants (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A, B).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNAi knockdown experiments shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A, B.

claim: Two classical guidance molecules, Slit and Netrin, have been shown to specifically bind to the extracellular domain of Dscam1.
source: Two classical guidance molecules, Slit and Netrin, have been shown to specifically bind to the extracellular domain of Dscam1 (Alavi et al., 2016; Andrews et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies on Dscam1 ligand binding.

claim: The Drosophila genome contains the sole slit gene and two Netrin genes: Netrin-A (NetA) and Netrin-B (NetB).
source: The Drosophila genome contains the sole slit gene and two Netrin genes: Netrin-A (NetA) and Netrin-B (NetB) (Harris et al., 1996; Mitchell et al., 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Harris et al., 1996 and Mitchell et al., 1996.

claim: Ubiquitous knockdown of both NetA and NetB resulted in the defective horizontal axon projection of s-LNvs.
source: Notably, ubiquitous knockdown of both NetA and NetB (hereafter referred to as Netrins), rather than slit, resulted in the defective horizontal axon projection of s-LNvs.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNAi knockdown experiments shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: NetA,NetB double mutant exhibited the defective horizontal axon projection of s-LNvs.
source: Convincingly, NetA,NetB double mutant (Brankatschk and Dickson, 2006), but not NetA or NetB single mutant, exhibited the defective horizontal axon projection of s-LNvs (Figure 4A, B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by genetic analysis of Netrin mutants shown in Figure 4A, B.

claim: NetA or NetB single mutants did not exhibit defective horizontal axon projection of s-LNvs.
source: Convincingly, NetA,NetB double mutant (Brankatschk and Dickson, 2006), but not NetA or NetB single mutant, exhibited the defective horizontal axon projection of s-LNvs (Figure 4A, B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by genetic analysis of Netrin mutants shown in Figure 4A, B.

claim: Two Netrin molecules function redundantly in regulating horizontal axon projection of s-LNvs.
source: These results imply that two Netrin molecules function redundantly in regulating horizontal axon projection of s-LNvs.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that only double mutants, not single mutants, show defects.

claim: When Netrins were knocked down in neurons but not in glia, severe defects in the horizontal axon projection of s-LNvs were observed.
source: Strikingly, when Netrins were knocked down in neurons but not in glia, we observed severe defects in the horizontal axon projection of s-LNvs.
evidence: This claim is supported by cell-type-specific knockdown experiments shown in Figure 4C, D.

claim: Neuron-secreted Netrins serve as ligands for Dscam1, controlling the horizontal axon projection of s-LNvs.
source: These findings reveal that neuron-secreted Netrins serve as ligands for Dscam1, controlling the horizontal axon projection of s-LNvs.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combination of experiments showing neuronal Netrin requirement and Dscam1 function.

claim: Knockdown of Netrins with OK107-GAL4 showed normal horizontal axon projection of s-LNvs.
source: We first excluded the possibility that MB-secreted Netrins mediate the horizontal axon projection of s-LNvs, as knockdown of Netrins with OK107-GAL4 showed normal horizontal axon projection of s-LNvs (Figure 5A, B).
evidence: This claim is supported by knockdown experiments shown in Figure 5A, B.

claim: Knockdown of Netrins in DNs resulted in the defective horizontal axon projection of s-LNvs.
source: Interestingly, knockdown of Netrins in a substantial portion of DN2, DN3, and DN1 (Kaneko et al., 1997) (Per-GAL4, Pdf-GAL80;UAS-Netrins-RNAi) resulted in the defective horizontal axon projection of s-LNvs (Figure 5A, B).
evidence: This claim is supported by cell-type-specific knockdown experiments shown in Figure 5A, B.

claim: The impairments in the horizontal axonal projection of s-LNvs due to DNs ablation were exclusively observed at 96 hr ALH.
source: Notably, the impairments in the horizontal axonal projection of s-LNvs due to DNs ablation were exclusively observed at 96 hr ALH, which is after the occurrence of horizontal projection (Figure 5C, D).
evidence: This claim is supported by temporal analysis of DN ablation effects shown in Figure 5C, D.

claim: Ablating crz+ neurons had no significant effects on the horizontal axon projection of the s-LNvs.
source: In contrast, ablating crz+ neurons, which occupy a similar location to DNs, had no significant effects on the horizontal axon projection of the s-LNvs (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by control ablation experiments shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Expressing NetB in DNs in NetA,NetB double mutants successfully restored the defective horizontal axon projection of s-LNvs.
source: Moreover, by expressing NetB in DNs in NetA,NetB double mutants, we successfully restored the defective horizontal axon projection of s-LNvs (NetABΔ;Per-GAL4, Pdf-GAL80;UAS-NetB) (Figure 5E, F).
evidence: This claim is supported by genetic rescue experiments shown in Figure 5E, F.

claim: DNs secrete Netrins to guide the horizontal axon projection of s-LNvs.
source: These results demonstrate that DNs secrete Netrins to guide the horizontal axon projection of s-LNvs.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combination of knockdown, ablation, and rescue experiments.

claim: The number of DNs significantly increased during the s-LNvs axon projection process.
source: Therefore, we monitored the number and location of DNs during the s-LNvs axon projection and found that the number of DNs significantly increased during this process.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis of DN numbers shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Per-GAL4, Pdf-GAL80; UAS-mCD8::GFP only labeled 4–5 cells at 48 hr ALH.
source: Per-GAL4, Pdf-GAL80; UAS-mCD8::GFP only labeled 4–5 cells at 48 hr ALH, and raise to 10–15 by 72 hr, and subsequently increased to approximately 25 by 96 hr ALH (Figure 6A, B).
evidence: This claim is supported by cell counting data shown in Figure 6A, B.

claim: DN numbers increased to 10–15 by 72 hr ALH.
source: Per-GAL4, Pdf-GAL80; UAS-mCD8::GFP only labeled 4–5 cells at 48 hr ALH, and raise to 10–15 by 72 hr, and subsequently increased to approximately 25 by 96 hr ALH (Figure 6A, B).
evidence: This claim is supported by cell counting data shown in Figure 6A, B.

claim: DN numbers increased to approximately 25 by 96 hr ALH.
source: Per-GAL4, Pdf-GAL80; UAS-mCD8::GFP only labeled 4–5 cells at 48 hr ALH, and raise to 10–15 by 72 hr, and subsequently increased to approximately 25 by 96 hr ALH (Figure 6A, B).
evidence: This claim is supported by cell counting data shown in Figure 6A, B.

claim: The location of newly formed DNs resides lateral to the transition point of axon projection direction of the s-LNvs.
source: It is worth noting that the location of these newly formed DNs resides lateral to the transition point of axon projection direction of the s-LNvs, while maintaining a basic parallelism with the horizontal axon projection of the s-LNvs (Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data showing the spatial relationship in Figure 6A.

claim: The sharp increase in the number of DNs coincides remarkably with the timing of the switch in axon projection direction of the s-LNvs.
source: The sharp increase in the number of DNs coincides remarkably with the timing of the switch in axon projection direction of the s-LNvs.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the temporal correlation between DN birth and axon projection direction change.

claim: At 72 hr ALH, no NetB signals were detected within the DNs.
source: At 72 hr ALH, we were unable to detect any NetB signals within the DNs.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: At 96 hr ALH, prominent NetB signals were detected in approximately six to eight newborn DNs.
source: In contrast, at 96 hr ALH, we easily detected prominent NetB signals in approximately six to eight newborn DNs (Figure 6C, D, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 6C, D.

claim: DSCAM is involved in Netrin-1-mediated axonal attraction.
source: Previous studies have shown that DSCAM is involved in Netrin-1-mediated axonal attraction (Andrews et al., 2008; Liu et al., 2009; Ly et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies on DSCAM function.

claim: DSCAM functions as a repulsive receptor, associating with UNC5C to mediate Netrin-1-induced axon growth cone collapse.
source: In addition, DSCAM also functions as a repulsive receptor, associating with Uncoordinated-5C (UNC5C) to mediate Netrin-1-induced axon growth cone collapse (Fernandez et al., 2020; Purohit et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Fernandez et al., 2020 and Purohit et al., 2012.

claim: Expression of either NetA or NetB in R78G02-GAL4-labeled neurons significantly suppressed the horizontal axon projection of s-LNvs.
source: Expression of either NetA or NetB in R78G02-GAL4-labeled neurons significantly suppressed the horizontal axon projection of s-LNvs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B, C).
evidence: This claim is supported by ectopic expression experiments shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B, C.

claim: Newborn DNs secrete Netrins to orchestrate the transition of axon projection in s-LNvs from a vertical to a horizontal direction.
source: Taken together, these findings reveal that newborn DNs secrete Netrins to orchestrate the transition of axon projection in s-LNvs from a vertical to a horizontal direction (Figure 7).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combination of all experimental results showing DN birth, Netrin expression, and effects on s-LNv projection.

claim: Intermediate targets play a pivotal role by providing vital guiding information that enables axons to transition their projection directions.
source: Crucially, intermediate targets play a pivotal role by providing vital guiding information that enables axons to transition their projection directions and embark upon the subsequent stages of their journey, ultimately leading them to their final destination (Bartoe et al., 2006; de Ramon Francàs et al., 2017; Stoeckli, 2018; Timofeev et al., 2012; Timofeev et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature on intermediate targets in axon guidance.

claim: The midline floor plate cells secrete long-range attractive signals to attract commissural axons toward them.
source: In vertebrates, the midline floor plate cells secrete long-range attractive signals to attract commissural axons toward them (Kennedy et al., 1994; Serafini et al., 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Kennedy et al., 1994 and Serafini et al., 1996.

claim: Floor plate cells emit signals of rejection to prevent excessive closeness of axons, aiding the axon in departing the floor plate.
source: Once there, these cells emit signals of rejection to prevent excessive closeness of axons, thus aiding the axon in departing the floor plate to reach its intended destination (Kidd et al., 1998; Long et al., 2004; Stoeckli et al., 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to studies on midline repulsion.

claim: The s-LNv axons originate from the ventrolateral soma and project to the dorsolateral area of the brain.
source: The s-LNv axons originate from the ventrolateral soma and project to the dorsolateral area of the brain, and subsequently undergo a axon projection direction shift, projecting horizontally toward the midline with a short dorsal extension (Helfrich-Förster et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Helfrich-Förster et al., 2007.

claim: Several factors including the Slit–Robo signal impact the axon outgrowth of s-LNvs in the adult flies' dorsal projection.
source: Several studies have reported the impact of various factors, including the Slit–Robo signal (Oliva et al., 2016), Unc5 (Fernandez et al., 2020), Lar (leukocyte-antigen-related) (Agrawal and Hardin, 2016), dfmr1 (Okray et al., 2015), dTip60 (Pirooznia et al., 2012), and Dscam1 long 3′ UTR (Zhang et al., 2019), on the axon outgrowth of s-LNvs in the adult flies' dorsal projection.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple previous studies.

claim: The vertical projection of s-LNv axons is dependent on MB calyx expansion.
source: Hence, the vertical projection of s-LNv axons is dependent on MB calyx expansion.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the correlation analysis and ablation experiments showing the relationship between MB and s-LNv vertical projection.

claim: In Drosophila, at the midline of the embryonic central nervous system, Dscam1 forms a complex with Robo1 to receive the Slit signal and promote the growth of longitudinal axons.
source: In Drosophila, at the midline of the embryonic central nervous system, Dscam1 forms a complex with Robo1 to receive the Slit signal and promote the growth of longitudinal axons (Alavi et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Alavi et al., 2016.

claim: In adult flies, Slit/Robo signaling restricts the medial growth of s-LNv axons.
source: In adult flies, Slit/Robo signaling restricts the medial growth of s-LNv axons (Oliva et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Oliva et al., 2016.

claim: Reducing Netrins levels led to a decrease in the horizontal projection distance of s-LNv axons.
source: However, we found that reducing Netrins levels, rather than slit, led to a decrease in the horizontal projection distance of s-LNv axons.
evidence: This claim is supported by knockdown experiments comparing Netrins and slit.

claim: In the NetABΔ double mutant, the extent of defects in the horizontal axonal projection of s-LNv neurons is similar to that observed when knocking down Dscam1 in s-LNvs.
source: Moreover, in the NetABΔ double mutant, the extent of defects in the horizontal axonal projection of s-LNv neurons is similar to that observed when knocking down Dscam1 in s-LNvs.
evidence: This claim is inferred from comparing the phenotypes of Netrin mutants and Dscam1 knockdown.

claim: Dscam1 has been shown to be involved as a receptor for Netrin in mediating axon growth and pathfinding.
source: Indeed, previous studies have provided evidence showcasing the widespread involvement of Dscam1 as a receptor for Netrin in mediating axon growth and pathfinding (Liu et al., 2009; Ly et al., 2008; Matthews and Grueber, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies on Dscam1-Netrin interactions.

claim: Disturbing the expression of Netrin signals in the axon targeting microenvironment was sufficient to cause abnormal s-LNv projection.
source: When we disturbed the expression of Netrin signals in the axon targeting microenvironment, it was also sufficient to cause abnormal s-LNv projection (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B, C).
evidence: This claim is supported by ectopic expression experiments shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B, C.

claim: Netrin, as a ligand for Dscam1, regulates the process of switching axon projection direction.
source: Therefore, our findings suggest that Netrin, as a ligand for Dscam1, regulates the process of switching axon projection direction (Figure 4).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combination of experiments showing Netrin and Dscam1 function in horizontal projection.

claim: Following vertical projection, the s-LNvs growth cones remain within the dorsolateral area for at least 48 hr before initiating horizontal projection.
source: Following vertical projection, the s-LNvs growth cones remain within the dorsolateral area for at least 48 hr before initiating horizontal projection (Figure 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by temporal analysis of axon projection shown in Figure 1.

claim: The dorsolateral area serves as an intermediate target to facilitate the subsequent phase of s-LNvs projection journey.
source: This phenomenon aligns harmoniously with the outcomes observed in earlier studies that the axonal growth of other types of neurons slows down at the specific choice point, the midline (Bak and Fraser, 2003; Godement et al., 1994; Li et al., 2021), indicating that the dorsolateral area serves as an intermediate targets to facilitate the subsequent phase of s-LNvs projection journey.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation of growth cone pausing and comparison to other systems.

claim: The axon terminals of s-LNvs showed close spatial associations with the somas and processes of DNs.
source: The axon terminals of s-LNvs showed close spatial associations with the somas and processes of DNs.
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data showing the spatial relationship between s-LNvs and DNs.

claim: The Netrin signaling microenvironment secreted by DNs is involved in regulating the horizontal projection of s-LNv axons.
source: These findings suggest that the Netrin signaling microenvironment secreted by DNs is involved in regulating the horizontal projection of s-LNv axons.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combination of knockdown and ablation experiments targeting DNs.

claim: The emergence of NetB-positive DNs and the aberrant axonal projection of s-LNv neurons caused by DN ablation occur concurrently during development.
source: The emergence of NetB-positive DNs and the aberrant axonal projection of s-LNv neurons caused by DN ablation occur concurrently during development (Figure 6).
evidence: This claim is supported by temporal analysis of DN birth and NetB expression shown in Figure 6.

claim: Three types of circadian oscillator neurons, including two DN1s, two DN2s, and four to five s-LNvs, can be identified as early as embryonic stage 16.
